items.question: What practice must accompany worship of this circle to produce its effect?
items.inference: Sustained meditation after worship activates the circle's power.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation for as long as one continues.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible through this meditative practice?
items.inference: The practice grants access to diverse languages, both familiar and unfamiliar.
uncertainties: Gender agreement between bhāṣās (f.) and aśrutāni/śrutāni (n.) is unusual but taken as describing the utterances.
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms, both unheard and heard, become manifest.

items.question: Where and by whom are these diverse languages heard in this experience?
items.inference: The perception of languages is entirely internal and self-generated.
items.plain_english: By oneself alone, through oneself, to oneself, and within oneself, they are heard.

items.question: What bodily transformation results from the successful practice of this circle?
premises: The practitioner becomes free of wrinkles and grey hair
The resemblance is as a second Kāma
items.inference: The practice confers youthful beauty comparable to the god of love.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he becomes a second god of love.

rows.grounds: object or source to be destroyed; compound vāyu-ādeḥ

items.question: What effect does destroying the wind and related forces have on speech?
premises: Wind and related forces are to be destroyed
items.inference: Suppressing the wind forces renders one silent like a mute.
uncertainties: The exact referent of vāyvādeḥ (wind element, breath, or hostile forces) is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: One should destroy the wind and so forth; then he indeed stands mute in speech.

items.question: What is the distinctive power attributed to the seventh circle?
items.inference: The seventh circle possesses the supreme power to paralyze armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme and causes the paralysis of armies.

items.question: What perceptual ability arises for one devoted to worship and meditation on that circle?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation
items.inference: Devotion to that circle grants the ability to see from a distance.
items.plain_english: Indeed, for one devoted to worship and meditation on that circle, there is vision from afar.

rows.grounds: names further magical acts; compound stambha-moha-ādikaṃ

items.question: What range of magical operations becomes possible through this circle's power?
items.inference: The circle enables a range of destructive and controlling magical operations.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and so forth become possible.

items.question: What knowledge is required for success in these ritual operations?
premises: The method of eight times eight must be known
items.inference: Mastery of the eight-times-eight method is necessary for success.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of the eight times eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

items.question: How should the teaching just given be received and ascertained by the listener?
premises: The teaching is declared without doubt
items.inference: The teaching is certain and should be ascertained through devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this has been declared by me without doubt; ascertain it with devotion and reasoning.

rows.grounds: locative descriptor of the text; compound candradvīpa-vinirgate

items.question: What textual division concludes at this point in the Candradvīpa teaching?
premises: The context is the Candradvīpa emergence
items.inference: This marks the end of the eighth chapter in the Candradvīpa section.
items.plain_english: In the teaching that emerged in Candradvīpa, this is the eighth chapter.

items.question: What new topic is the speaker about to explain to the beloved listener?
premises: The speaker intends to tell something
The topic is the arrangement of yoginī rows
The listener is addressed as beloved
items.inference: The speaker will now explain the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

items.question: What collective domain encompasses all earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs?
premises: They form a complete field group
items.inference: All earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs together constitute the complete field group.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of sarvakṣetrakam as a standalone nominative in this fragmentary verse is somewhat elliptical.
items.plain_english: This is the complete field group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

rows.grounds: describes a class of yoginīs; compound sarva-sahajāḥ
describes a class of yoginīs; compound sarva-kulajā
describes a class of yoginīs; compound sarva-dvāra-pālikāḥ

items.question: Which categories of yoginīs are included in this comprehensive enumeration?
items.inference: The enumeration covers innate, family-born, and door-guardian yoginīs.
uncertainties: sarvakulajā appears as singular in form but is read as a collective plural in this list.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all the family-born ones, and all the door-guardians.

items.question: Why has the supreme secret among all secrets been revealed to the listener?
premises: It is the supreme secret among secrets
The revelation is due to the listener's devotion
items.inference: The listener's devotion warrants the revelation of the supreme secret.
items.plain_english: Because of your devotion, the supreme secret of secrets has been revealed.

items.question: What further instruction does the listener now request from the gurus?
premises: The listener expresses a wish now
The topic is the worship of siddhas from the gurus
items.inference: The listener requests instruction on the worship of siddhas as taught by the gurus.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: To whom should the arrangement of the two syllables be imparted?
premises: There is an arrangement of two syllables
It should be given among others
items.inference: The two-syllable arrangement should be imparted to others as prescribed.
uncertainties: The meaning of anyanteṣu is obscure; it may refer to other recipients or other contexts.
items.plain_english: One should impart the arrangement of the two syllables among others.

items.question: What claim is made about the uniqueness of this knowledge in the future?
premises: This knowledge is taken as the standard
No equal knowledge will arise again
items.inference: This knowledge is declared unsurpassed and never to be equaled in the future.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What specific instruction about those beings is the speaker about to deliver?
premises: The topic is the method of their names
The listener is urged to hear
items.inference: The speaker will explain the method of naming those beings.
items.plain_english: I shall speak the method of their names; listen, O beautiful-eyed one.

rows.grounds: designation or name element; compound catur-yuga

items.question: How are the independent impellers of the family identified in relation to the four ages?
premises: They are impellers of the family
items.inference: The independent impellers of the family are designated in connection with the four ages.
uncertainties: The precise syntactic relation of caturyuga iti to the rest of the verse is elliptical.
items.plain_english: Thus, O lord of gods, they are called the four ages, the independent impellers of the family.

rows.grounds: describes extent of kaulaṃ; compound daśa-koṭi-pramāṇaṃ

items.question: What is the extent and origin attributed to this Kaula teaching?
items.inference: This Kaula teaching is vast in extent and of supreme origin.
uncertainties: The unit implied by daśakoṭi (verses, mantras, or beings) is not specified.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, measuring ten crores, is supremely arisen.

items.question: By what agency and to what extent does the yoginī named Will operate?
premises: Her operation extends up to māyā by supreme will
items.inference: The yoginī named Will, through the siddhas and supreme will, operates up to the limit of māyā.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of siddhaiḥ and māyāntaṃ is compressed and open to interpretation.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Will, by the siddhas and by supreme will, extends up to māyā.

rows.grounds: genitive indicating recipients or subject matter

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching concerning the mothers in this lineage?
items.inference: The sky-movers transmitted the teaching concerning the mothers.
items.plain_english: Again, O goddess, O beloved, it was told by the sky-movers concerning the mothers.

rows.grounds: genitive indicating recipients or subject matter

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving yoginīs who are good eaters?
premises: They are described as good eaters
items.inference: An earth-mover transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving yoginīs who are good eaters.
uncertainties: The meaning of subhakṣāṇāṃ ('good eaters' or 'having good food/offerings') is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: O beloved, it was told by an earth-mover to the earth-moving yoginīs, the good eaters.
